usds-sky.title: How does USDS break?
usds-sky.thesis: Capture the vote queue, wait out the 48-hour delay, then mint USDS or replace the token; holders can cash out only 4.39 billion.
usds-sky.premise: Hypothetical: one coalition accumulates more SKY approvals than the sitting hat and lifts itself into control of the Sky Chief. No compromise, coercion or misconduct by any voter, delegate, signer or custodian is alleged, and no such capture has been observed. Everything else in the route - the 48-hour delay, the governor's authority over the USDS token, the LitePSM's USDC stock and the Vow's empty cushion - was read or replayed at block 26,139,200 on 2026-10-07. Figures covering the collateral book are shared with DAI and are never USDS-only.

stages.title: Outvote the sitting hat
stages.action: Lock SKY in the Chief, vote for a slate carrying one spell contract, then lift it
stages.cost: One block of voting; the SKY is escrowed, not spent
stages.missingDefense: No quorum of people, no signature threshold and no committee: only relative weight
stages.explanation: Chief.canCall authorises exactly one address, the current hat, and lift installs any address holding strictly more approvals. At the pinned block the hat held 7.04bn SKY of approvals - 30.0% of supply - and 7.16bn SKY sat escrowed in the Chief. The cost to outvote it is its live approval weight, which changes with staking and voting; the pinned figure is not a fixed threshold. The lift cooldown is 10 blocks, so displacing the hat takes a single transaction once the approvals exist.

stages.title: Queue one spell
stages.action: DSPause.plot(spell, codehash, calldata, eta) with eta at or after now + 172800
stages.missingDefense: The only caller is the authority the route already took
stages.explanation: plot is gated to the Chief hat through Chief.canCall, and it rejects any eta earlier than now + delay. A fork replay recorded three attempts: plot from a non-hat address reverted, plot from the hat one second short of the delay reverted, and plot at exactly now + 172800 succeeded and emitted the LogNote event.

stages.title: Wait out 48 hours
stages.action: The queued plan sits in DSPause.plans until its eta
stages.missingDefense: No veto, no cancellation by anyone but the attacker's own hat
stages.explanation: This is the whole defence the delay buys: visibility. drop is auth-gated to that same hat, so no guardian, holder, delegate or committee can cancel the plan, and re-plotting one is equally impossible for them. The replay measured the delay exactly: exec one second before eta reverted and exec at eta succeeded, 172,800 seconds of chain time after the plot block.

stages.title: Execute the spell
stages.action: DSPause.exec(spell, codehash, calldata, eta)
stages.cost: One transaction, and any address may send it
stages.missingDefense: No post-execution check beyond the proxy still owning itself
stages.explanation: exec carries no authorization beyond a plan that was plotted and a codehash that still matches, so nothing needs to be signed at execution time: the replay executed the plan from an unrelated address once eta had passed. The delegatecall runs in the PauseProxy's own storage context, so the spell's calls reach USDS with the governor as msg.sender and as address(this).

stages.title: Mint or replace USDS
stages.action: Usds.rely(newMinter) then Usds.mint(to, amount), or upgradeToAndCall(newImplementation)
stages.missingDefense: No supply cap, no mint delay and no second governor
stages.explanation: A replay impersonating the governor at the pinned block confirmed all three capabilities and their limits. The governor is already a ward: rely added a new minter, mint created 1,000,000 USDS to an address carrying no code, the newly relied address then minted on its own, and upgradeToAndCall accepted an implementation address. The same mint from a non-ward reverted with Usds/not-authorized, and a burn of a holder's balance without an allowance also reverted - the token gives the governor issuance and logic control but no seizure.

stages.title: Redeem the PSM stock
stages.action: UsdsPsmWrapper.buyGem(recipient, gemAmt) takes USDC from the LitePSM pocket at par
stages.cost: One transaction per holder, no fee
stages.missingDefense: Inventory, not solvency: the pocket is one issuer's token sitting in one contract
stages.explanation: The wrapper converts USDS one-for-one into the joined DAI the LitePSM accepts and pays out USDC from the pocket, whose entire balance is reachable by public calls. The replay took 1,000,000 USDS to exactly 1,000,000 USDC with tin and tout at zero, showed that asking for one unit more than the pocket reverts, drained the remaining $4.390bn pocket in a single call, and then showed the next exit reverting on an empty pocket. Against $7.122bn of USDS that is 61.7% of supply, and 37.5% of the USDS plus DAI book.

stages.title: Hold the leftover claim
stages.action: Everyone still holding keeps a claim on the shared collateral book
stages.explanation: USDS exposes no pause, freeze, blacklist or admin transfer, so holders cannot be locked out of the token, and the governor cannot debit a balance without that holder's allowance. The residual problem is economic: the $2.731bn of USDS the pocket cannot cash is a claim on a shared book whose largest measured ilk positions were 43.8% LitePSM USDC, 32.1% Spark lending and 14.4% Bloom at the pin, and the Vow held no surplus to absorb an uncovered gap.

window.label: Notice window, not a defence window
window.note: The delay is enforced at plot and at exec and cannot be shortened by anyone but the sitting hat. It publishes the plan and buys two days of notice, but it grants no veto: the only address that can drop a queued plan is the hat that queued it.

defenders.name: The 48-hour delay
defenders.why: It enforces public notice and prevents same-block execution, and the replay measured it exactly at 172,800 seconds of chain time. It is not a veto: cancellation is auth-gated to the same hat, and execution needs no further authorization, so the delay only changes when the outcome lands.

defenders.name: Voting holders
defenders.why: Displacing the hat requires strictly more than its live SKY approvals - 7.04bn at the pin - which is a real but moving cost, and a later hat can drop a plan the previous one queued. Neither helps inside the 48 hours, and acquiring the stake is a market transaction rather than a control that blocks the route.

defenders.name: Emergency Shutdown Module
defenders.why: fire() requires Sum to reach min, and min is set to 2^256-1 while the module held 0.001306 MKR of the legacy governance token. The threshold is unreachable by any amount of staking, so emergency shutdown cannot be triggered at all.

defenders.name: The End shutdown module
defenders.why: live reads 1 and the module is wired as a ward of the Vat, Dog, Spot and Vow. Its only callers are the ESM, which cannot fire, and MCD_PAUSE_PROXY, which this route already controls, so caging the system is another thing the captured authority can do rather than something that stops it.

defenders.name: The LitePSM
defenders.why: It returns cash at par with no fee and its $4.391bn pocket is reachable in full, covering 61.7% of USDS supply. That is an inventory bound on one issuer's token held by one contract, not a solvency guarantee, and the same issuer can disable it outright.

defenders.name: The Vow surplus
defenders.why: At the pin the Vow held $0.654bn of surplus against $0.715bn of recognised debt, a net shortfall of $0.060bn, with a further $0.228bn in the debt queue. Both auction levers are disabled by configuration: bump is zero and hump and sump are max uint256, so neither a surplus auction nor a debt auction can start.

defenders.name: Circle
defenders.why: USDC was live and the PSM pocket was not blacklisted at the pin, and the blacklister is an on-chain role. A fork replay showed blacklisting the pocket reverts both swap directions on the LitePSM with the issuer's own reason string, which removes the last cash exit instead of absorbing the loss.

falsifiers.condition: The sitting hat differs from the recorded 0xF01b594aF26fC8A8ae1e24DCaF904ECB6Fd1BaDC, Chief.lift loses its strict comparison approvals[candidate] > approvals[hat], or the Chief-authorized DSPause route to the recorded PauseProxy changes
DSPause.delay falls below 172,800 seconds, or plot accepts an eta earlier than now + delay
USDS gains a pause, freeze, blacklist or admin seizure over holder balances
The Emergency Shutdown Module can still fire, because min is reachable staked MKR
A guardian, committee or second authority can cancel or veto a queued spell
The Vow holds any net surplus at all, with Vat credit exceeding Vat debt; at the pinned block it holds none
The LitePSM replenishes its USDC stock from a source other than the Circle issuer
The collateral book's Spark, Bloom and Grove positions are fully looked through to named assets

exposure.label: USDS holders
exposure.detail: $7.122bn of USDS was outstanding at block 26,139,200, and DAI added $4.587bn of claims on the same book, so the shared liability base was $11.709bn.

exposure.detail: 35 ilks carried $11.851bn of Vat debt in total, against a Vat debt of $12.566bn including $0.715bn of unbacked debt. Measured ilk shares were 43.8% LitePSM USDC, 32.1% Spark, 14.4% Bloom and 1.0% Grove. These are shared DAO-wide figures, not USDS-only reserves.

exposure.label: Cash reachable at par
exposure.detail: The LitePSM pocket held $4.391bn of USDC with tin and tout at zero and $0.798bn of pre-minted DAI held. A public call drained the remaining pocket at par; the next exited reverted. That is 61.7% of USDS supply and 37.5% of combined USDS and DAI supply.

exposure.detail: sUSDS reported $4.934bn of total assets against 4.437bn sUSDS shares, so a large share of outstanding USDS is itself wrapped and would run through the same exit.

exposure.label: Absorption capacity
exposure.detail: Dog's global auction cap Hole was $150m with Dirt at zero, and the Vow had no surplus. Liquidation throughput is capped, and uncovered debt has nowhere to go while hump and sump are max uint256.

crvusd-curve.title: How does crvUSD break?
crvusd-curve.thesis: Three Safe keys bypass vlCVX voting; one operator-delegate key needs a poll majority whose size depends on outside veCRV opposition.
crvusd-curve.premise: Hypothetical: three of the five signers on Convex's vote-extension Safe, or one ConvexCore operator key, are compromised, coerced, or collude. No such compromise has been observed. At block 26,138,725, the one-key route needs 55.48% poll yes when other veCRV abstains, or 94.31% against all outside opposition; both routes require an early, full-weight Curve ballot.

stages.title: Open a malicious vote
stages.actor: Any address holding at least 2,500 veCRV
stages.action: Ownership Voting newVote(script: DAO Agent → Factory admin → set_debt_ceiling(attacker, X))
stages.missingDefense: Proposal creation is open to any holder above the veCRV minimum
stages.explanation: The vote can be opened before or after the keys are taken. Its script tells the DAO Agent to raise a debt ceiling for an address the attacker controls. The vote is public from its first block.

stages.title: Wait out the vote
stages.action: Seven-day vote period runs to completion
stages.missingDefense: Execution cannot be brought forward: the 7-day period must elapse first
stages.explanation: On the Safe route Convex's whole weight is cast yes directly, whatever vlCVX holders wanted. Curve requires yes votes to exceed 51% of votes cast and 30% of total voting power, so at block 26,138,725 (a 54.0798% share) no combination of other holders could put it below either bar. The vote still cannot be executed while it is open: a fork replay confirmed executeVote reverts until the full seven-day period has elapsed.

stages.title: Execute and mint
stages.action: executeVote → DAO Agent → Factory admin.execute → set_debt_ceiling(attacker, X) → crvUSD.mint(attacker, X)
stages.cost: One transaction, once the vote period has elapsed
stages.missingDefense: No collateral check, no further timelock
stages.explanation: Raising a debt ceiling mints the increase straight to the named address. A fork replay of exactly this script minted 10 million crvUSD to a plain address: no collateral, no registered lending market, and no allowance or co-signature from the recipient.

stages.title: Sell into the peg
stages.action: Swap the unbacked crvUSD into Curve pools, PegKeeper pairs and LlamaLend markets
stages.explanation: crvUSD holders, scrvUSD depositors and LlamaLend lenders are left holding a claim with no matching collateral.

branches.label: Through the Safe
branches.premise: Three of the five signers on the Safe that owns Convex's vote extension are compromised, coerced, or collude.

stages.title: Take three Safe keys
stages.action: Obtain 3 of 5 signatures on the Safe that owns Convex's vote extension
stages.missingDefense: No Safe guard, no modules: three signatures are enough
stages.explanation: The Safe is a plain 3-of-5 with no guard and no modules, so any three owners can sign any call it is allowed to make.

stages.title: Swap the vote caster
stages.action: VoteDelegateExtension.setDaoOperator(attacker)
stages.missingDefense: No timelock · no vlCVX approval · two hand-off paths
stages.explanation: The Booster only accepts votes from this extension, and the extension's owner can name any address as the caster, effective immediately. Today the caster is CurveVoteExecutor, which applies the vlCVX result; nothing obliges the owner to keep it. The Safe drove this role directly from 2022 until it appointed the executor on 2026-08-03. A second path (revertControl, then the Booster owner) also hands over the delegate, so a guard on setDaoOperator alone would not close this route.

stages.title: Vote all veCRV yes
stages.action: DaoVote(voteId, true) → Booster → VoterProxy → Voting.vote
stages.missingDefense: The vlCVX result is never consulted
stages.explanation: The replacement caster votes the whole pooled position at once. The cvxCRV holders whose CRV is locked there cannot withdraw it or redirect its vote.

branches.label: Via ConvexCore
branches.premise: Hypothetical operator-delegate compromise: at block 26,138,725 and full-weight voting, the poll needs at least 55.48% yes if other veCRV abstains, or 94.31% to withstand all outside opposition.

stages.title: Take the operator key
stages.action: Obtain control of the operator EOA 0x947B7742C403f20e5FaCcDAc5E092C943E7D0277
stages.cost: Off-chain compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.missingDefense: One operator can make ConvexCore call anything; no second operator or timelock
stages.explanation: ConvexCore's three operators are this EOA, a 3-of-5 Safe and FxGaugeExecutor: they are not three interchangeable keys, and the EOA alone can drive ConvexCore. At block 26,138,725 it also held delegated weight equal to 45.8% of vlCVX, while its own locked balance was zero.

stages.title: Rig a one-day poll
stages.actor: ConvexCore, called by the compromised key
stages.action: ConvexCore.execute(platform, createProposal(start, end, Ownership, curveVoteId)) · ConvexCore.execute(executor, setGuardian(operatorEOA, true))
stages.cost: Two transactions; the poll stays open at least one day and must open a day before the Curve vote's half-way point
stages.missingDefense: No timelock on poll creation or guardian appointment; the guardian only skips the 12-hour finalization wait
stages.explanation: ConvexCore owns both contracts, so the key can bind a poll to any Curve vote id and mark itself guardian. It cannot replace the executor's fixed pointers, forge holder ballots, or skip the poll: a fork run showed the executor still sends the platform's proportional result.

stages.title: Win the conditional poll
stages.action: DaoVotePlatform.vote(platformProposalId, operatorEOA, 10000, 0)
stages.cost: One transaction; no vlCVX purchase needed
stages.missingDefense: No cap on delegated concentration
stages.explanation: At block 26,138,725, a full yes ballot from the operator's 45.8% delegated vlCVX block tolerates about 36.77% of supply voting no only if other veCRV abstains. Winning against all outside veCRV opposition instead needs at least 94.31% poll yes, allowing only about 2.76% of vlCVX supply to vote no.

stages.title: Cast the proportional split
stages.action: CurveVoteExecutor.executeDaoVote(platformProposalId) → extension.DaoVoteWithWeights(curveVoteId, yayBps, nayBps, true) → Booster → VoterProxy → Ownership Voting.vote
stages.cost: One transaction after the poll closes; it must land within the Curve vote's first 3.5 days
stages.missingDefense: No independent ballot veto
stages.explanation: The executor casts Convex's weight in the poll's proportion, floored to basis points. At the pinned share and full weight, 55.48% yes passes with other veCRV abstaining but can lose against opposition; 94.31% puts more than 51% of total veCRV in the yes column and passed on a fork with 15.2% outside veCRV voting no.

window.label: Public vote window
window.note: Visible onchain from the first block. No independent veto exists in the verified Voting → Agent → Factory path. On the ConvexCore route a counted no reduces the Curve yes, and undelegated holders can oppose during the poll; the Safe route bypasses that tally entirely. Exiting is an economic response, not the only option.

defenders.name: Other veCRV holders
defenders.why: They can defeat the weaker ConvexCore poll result. At the pinned share and full weight, the Safe's all-yes ballot or ConvexCore's 94.31% poll yes outvotes them at any turnout; 55.48% does not.

defenders.name: vlCVX holders
defenders.why: They cannot stop the Safe's caster replacement. At block 26,138,725, assuming the delegate votes its whole block yes, ConvexCore needs at least 55.48% poll yes if other veCRV abstains (opposing vlCVX no greater than about 36.77% of supply), or 94.31% to win against all outside veCRV opposition (no greater than about 2.76%); exceeding the latter removes immunity, not necessarily passage. ConvexCore can obstruct some delegated voters, but a fork run showed an undelegated holder could still vote no.

defenders.name: vlCVX delegators
defenders.why: In the current configuration they can vote directly during a running poll and pull their weight out of a delegate's ballot, but ConvexCore can zero the delegation gas limit and re-sync a holder so that a later direct vote reverts. It is an obstructable defence against the ConvexCore route only, not against the Safe.

defenders.name: Convex's two other signers
defenders.why: Two signatures cannot override three, and they have no say over a ConvexCore operator key.

defenders.name: Curve Emergency DAO
defenders.why: Its 5-of-9 Safe can pause PegKeepers, adjust market risk settings and reduce existing debt ceilings, but has no vote-cancel, Agent or Factory-mint veto in the Voting → Agent → Factory path. A fork replay showed the ceiling reduction reverts unless the holder approved the Factory, and tokens already sold to third parties cannot be recovered from them.

defenders.name: The market
defenders.why: The vote is public for seven days, so holders can leave early, but a mass exit is itself a depeg.

falsifiers.condition: The vote extension is owned by a vlCVX-controlled timelock, or ownership is renounced
setDaoOperator, and the revertControl hand-off to the Booster owner, gain an onchain delay that vlCVX holders can veto
The Safe gets a guard that blocks or delays both caster hand-off paths
ConvexCore's operators are replaced by a timelocked multi-signature authority
Convex holds 51% of veCRV or less at a vote snapshot
set_debt_ceiling stops minting to arbitrary addresses

usdc-circle.title: How does USDC break?
usdc-circle.thesis: A bank-reserve shock outlasts Circle's liquidity and public rescue, leaving holders unable to exit at par.
usdc-circle.premise: Hypothetical: a banking shock traps reserve cash, redemptions queue, and neither Circle nor public authorities restores access before confidence fails. USDC recovered after the March 2023 SVB shock; this scenario is the tail where it does not. No current bank failure, reserve shortfall or redemption suspension is asserted. August's examined reserves still included net cash and settlement balances, but individual bank exposures were undisclosed.

stages.title: Reserve banks fail
stages.action: A correlated bank failure or legal hold interrupts access to reserve cash
stages.missingDefense: Guaranteed deposit access
stages.explanation: Circle's August examination classified $10.60B as net cash and settlement balances, without individual bank shares. The scenario assumes enough cash becomes inaccessible to exceed available liquidity; that is not an observed loss.

stages.title: Cash access stalls
stages.action: Reserve assets cannot all become usable settlement cash immediately
stages.cost: Until bank access or replacement funding resumes
stages.missingDefense: Independent settlement backstop
stages.explanation: In 2023, $3.3B at SVB needed a public deposit backstop before becoming fully available. Today's reserve includes short Treasuries and overnight Treasury-backed repos, but their reported values do not prove uninterrupted payment access.

stages.title: Redemptions meet a gate
stages.action: Submit cash redemption requests through Circle's institutional account and banking channels
stages.cost: Banking and account processing; no measured stress deadline
stages.missingDefense: Universal direct redemption
stages.explanation: Outside the EEA, holders need an eligible Circle Mint account to redeem directly, and Mint currently serves institutions. Terms permit qualifying delays or suspensions; EEA holders have separate MiCA rights, not this same account-only contract.

stages.title: Holders sell the discount
stages.action: Sell USDC into stablecoin pools while cash arbitrage is impaired
stages.missingDefense: Continuous cash arbitrage
stages.explanation: A static 10M USDC sale into the sampled Uniswap USDC/USDT pool quotes 9.08M USDT, with a post-swap marginal ratio near 0.432. This measures one pool's depth, not a forecast; arbitrage and liquidity changes are excluded.

stages.title: DeFi inherits the shock
stages.action: USDC holdings and shared exit routes transmit the discount into other positions
stages.cost: Depends on protocol response and reserve recovery
stages.missingDefense: Independent backing cash
stages.explanation: Sky's LitePSM pocket holds 4.39B USDC, and seven sampled Curve and Uniswap pools hold another 78.54M. Those are measured token holdings, not predicted losses; DAI and USDS share Sky's exposure rather than owning separate copies.

stages.title: The rescue falls short
stages.action: Replacement liquidity, deposit recovery and market buying fail to restore timely par exits
stages.missingDefense: Committed full-loss backstop
stages.explanation: The Fed, Treasury and FDIC protected SVB depositors in 2023, and USDC recovered. This tail requires that a new rescue is absent, too slow or insufficient; the prior intervention does not establish a standing guarantee.

stages.title: Par exits stay unavailable
stages.action: Sell below par or wait for reserve access and recovery
stages.elapsed: T+days to an unknown recovery date
stages.cost: Discount or prolonged illiquidity; loss depends on recovery
stages.missingDefense: Certain timely reserve recovery
stages.explanation: An access shock can cause prolonged illiquidity without a permanent reserve loss. If reserve losses also exceed replacement funding, holders face impairment; Circle's 2025 filing separately warned that even successful reserve claims could be delayed in issuer insolvency.

window.label: Redemption queue
window.duration: Hours to days; no verified upper bound
window.note: Access restored or sufficient replacement funding supplied during this window arrests the chain. The 2023 intervention did so; no present stress-throughput measurement fixes the deadline.

defenders.name: Circle
defenders.why: Can mobilize accessible reserves, replacement banks and corporate liquidity. Whether those resources cover a correlated cash-access shock is not established by the monthly examination.

defenders.name: Treasury, Fed and FDIC
defenders.why: Full deposit access arrested the SVB route in 2023. A comparable intervention can arrest this chain, but future coverage and timing are discretionary rather than promised to USDC holders.

defenders.name: Market arbitrageurs
defenders.why: Can buy discounted USDC when they expect accessible par redemption. If cash access or recovery is doubtful, pool liquidity and market buying do not themselves restore bank reserves.

defenders.name: Circle transfer controls
defenders.why: The deployed pauser can stop transfers and the blacklister can freeze addresses. USDC was unpaused and the LitePSM pocket was not blacklisted at the pin; local fork replays verified both controls.

falsifiers.condition: Reserve bank deposits and net cash exposure are removed, with independently verified continuity of Treasury and repo settlement access.
Every non-EEA holder gains enforceable direct redemption without an institutional Circle Mint eligibility gate.
Named bank exposures and tested replacement liquidity demonstrate that the modeled correlated access loss can be met in full.
A binding standing backstop guarantees timely access to all affected reserve deposits and settlement channels.

exposure.label: Ethereum scope
exposure.detail: 49.05B USDC is Ethereum token totalSupply at the pin. It is not a measurement of global circulating supply, cross-chain balances or cash available for redemption.

exposure.label: Sky pocket holding
exposure.detail: LitePSM's reported pocket holds 4.39B USDC. Its gem points to Ethereum USDC, deposit and withdrawal fees were zero, and the pocket was not blacklisted at the pin.

exposure.label: Sampled pool inventory
exposure.detail: Three Curve pools and four Uniswap V3 pools hold 78.54M USDC in total. The sample is not an exhaustive DeFi inventory or a ranking of current venues.

exposure.label: Static exit quotes
exposure.detail: Selling 100M USDC into Curve 3pool quotes 63.20M USDT. Quotes isolate each pinned pool with unchanged liquidity and no external arbitrage; USDT, DAI and crvUSD outputs are tokens, not guaranteed dollars.

exposure.label: Off-chain reserve access
exposure.detail: August reserves were 18.01% short Treasuries, 67.55% overnight Treasury repo and 14.44% net cash/settlement balances. The 2025 filing named BNY custody and qualified reserve protection in issuer bankruptcy; neither proves current bank concentration.

gho-aave.title: How does GHO break?
gho-aave.thesis: Two of three Risk Council keys double a mint bucket and issue 310 million GHO to any address, with no deposit and no delay.
gho-aave.premise: Hypothetical: two of the three signers on Aave's Risk Council Safe are compromised, coerced, or collude. No such compromise has been observed, and no misconduct by any signer is alleged. The route needs nothing else: the permissions, the full bucket and the elapsed cooldown were all in place at the pinned block.

stages.title: Take two Council keys
stages.action: Obtain 2 of 3 signatures on the Aave Risk Council Safe
stages.cost: Off-chain: phishing, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.missingDefense: No Safe guard and no modules: two signatures are enough
stages.explanation: The Safe is a plain two-of-three with no guard, no module guard and no modules, so any two owners can sign any call it is permitted to make. A fork replay confirmed that one approval reverts and two execute.

stages.title: Double the mint bucket
stages.action: GhoBucketSteward.updateFacilitatorBucketCapacity(mainnet GSM facilitator, 620,000,000 GHO)
stages.missingDefense: No vote and no execution timelock on the increase
stages.explanation: This facilitator's bucket was already full at the pinned block, so the mint needs headroom first. The steward lets the Council at most double a capacity, and only once per day, but the day had already passed: the last increase was 119 days earlier. Raising the cap mints nothing by itself.

stages.title: Mint to any address
stages.action: GhoDirectFacilitator.mint(recipient, 310,000,000 GHO) → GhoToken.mint
stages.cost: One transaction, same block as the cap raise
stages.missingDefense: No collateral check and no restriction on the recipient
stages.explanation: The verified facilitator forwards the caller's chosen recipient and amount straight to the token. A fork replay minted 310 million GHO to a fresh address that held nothing and had no code: total supply rose from 699 million to 1.009 billion, and no collateral moved.

stages.title: Double again next day
stages.action: Raise the capacity again once a day has elapsed, then mint the new headroom
stages.missingDefense: No lifetime budget: the cap only limits the rate
stages.explanation: The cooldown bounds one mint, not the total. On the fork the same pair of calls one day later took the outstanding unbacked balance to 930 million GHO and supply to 1.629 billion, with no aggregate ceiling reached.

stages.title: Sell into thin exits
stages.action: Redeem through the mainnet GSM, then sell the remainder into the GHO pools
stages.missingDefense: Redemption stock is a fraction of a single day's mint
stages.explanation: On-chain quotes at the pinned block cover at least 24.7 million GHO at 98% or more of nominal token par: 22.5 million through the stablecoin module's remaining inventory and 2.2 million across the Curve, Uniswap v3 and Uniswap v4 pools. That is under 8% of one day's mint; the quoted stablecoin outputs are not guaranteed dollars.

stages.title: Governance arrives late
stages.action: Level-1 payload revokes MINTER_ROLE and zeroes the facilitator's bucket capacity
stages.cost: A full proposal, vote and executor delay
stages.missingDefense: No emergency path to the facilitator or the token
stages.explanation: The measured Level-1 path is a one-day voting cooldown, three days of voting and a one-day executor delay. A fork replay showed what it buys: future mints stop, but nothing is burned, the facilitator cannot even be removed while its level is non-zero, and revoking the mint role still leaves the Council able to raise capacities.

stages.title: Holders absorb the loss
stages.action: Savings depositors, stakers and pool holders are left with a claim no asset answers
stages.explanation: GHO has no pause, freeze, blacklist or recovery path, so the new units stay where they land and the loss falls on whoever holds the token when the issuance becomes known.

window.label: Unopposed issuance window
window.note: The mint is visible from its first block, but nothing can be executed against it sooner than the measured Level-1 governance path. Within that window the Council can repeat the doubling once a day. Exiting is an economic response, not a defence.

defenders.name: The third Council signer
defenders.why: One signature cannot block two on a two-of-three Safe that carries no guard and no modules.

defenders.name: Aave governance
defenders.why: It holds every relevant admin role but its fastest measured route is four days or more. A fork replay showed it can stop later mints, yet it cannot burn or freeze what exists, cannot remove a facilitator whose level is non-zero, and must revoke the mint role and the steward permission separately.

defenders.name: Aave governance guardians
defenders.why: Neither guardian holds any role on the facilitator, the token or the steward at the pinned block, and their cancellation powers sit on proposals and payloads, which this route never uses.

defenders.name: The GHO token
defenders.why: The deployed token is immutable and exposes no pause, freeze, blacklist, recovery or admin burn. Probes for all six on a fork reverted, and the only burn debits the facilitator's own balance, which is empty after it mints to someone else.

defenders.name: stkGHO and Umbrella
defenders.why: The Safety Module held 30.56 million GHO at the pinned block, and the Core market's Umbrella registry entry was empty. Either way these cover a lending-market deficit, which deposit-free facilitator issuance never creates.

defenders.name: The stablecoin module
defenders.why: Both mainnet modules were live and unfrozen, but their remaining inventory redeems only 22.5 million GHO. Freezing them is the one lever available quickly, and it removes the redemption venue rather than the issuance.

defenders.name: The market
defenders.why: The mint is public from its first block, so holders can try to leave, but measured depth runs out well before a single day's issuance and a mass exit is itself a depeg.

The Risk Council is no longer the Bucket Steward's risk council, or that facilitator leaves the controlled list

usde-ethena.title: How does USDe break?
usde-ethena.thesis: Five Safe signatures can repoint the minter, minting USDe with no collateral and no supply cap.
usde-ethena.premise: Hypothetical: five of the ten signers on Ethena's governance Safe, or their keys, are compromised or collude, and a whitelisted transaction executor relays the signed calls. No such compromise has been observed. The same five keys then schedule, wait out and execute one timelocked operation that replaces the token minter, so the replacement can issue USDe without collateral, outside every per-block limit EthenaMinting V2 enforces.

stages.title: Take five Safe keys
stages.action: Obtain 5 of 10 signatures on the Ethena governance Safe
stages.missingDefense: No Safe module, no independent co-signer: five keys are enough
stages.explanation: The Safe is a plain 5-of-10 with no modules. Its transaction guard restricts how a call may be relayed, not which signed call goes out, so five owners can authorise any call the Safe is permitted to make. This premise is hypothetical and no compromise has been observed.

stages.title: Schedule the minter swap
stages.action: TimelockController.schedule(USDe, 0, setMinter(attacker), 0, salt, 86400)
stages.missingDefense: The proposer and the canceller are the same five-of-ten Safe
stages.explanation: The Safe is the timelock's only proposer and canceller. The call is queued with a 24-hour delay and emits a public CallScheduled event carrying the operation id, target, calldata and delay, so the pending swap is observable from the first block.

stages.title: Wait out the delay
stages.action: 24-hour minimum delay before execution
stages.missingDefense: Nobody outside the Safe can veto: cancelling needs the same five keys
stages.explanation: The delay cannot be shortened on the spot: the timelock holds its own default-admin role, and a schedule with a shorter delay reverts. A fork replay confirmed execute reverts with the operation still pending and, after the delay, succeeds.

stages.title: Execute the swap
stages.actor: Compromised Safe or any whitelisted executor
stages.action: TimelockController.execute → USDe.setMinter(attacker)
stages.missingDefense: No guard, delay or review on the token's owner-only minter setter
stages.explanation: Executing the queued call replaces the minter and emits MinterUpdated. A fork replay of exactly this sequence repointed the minter to a plain address and left the token's owner unchanged.

stages.title: Mint without collateral
stages.action: USDe.mint(attacker, amount)
stages.missingDefense: The token mint checks only the caller: no collateral, no cap, no window
stages.explanation: USDe.mint only requires the caller to be the stored minter. On the fork the replacement minted one billion USDe to an empty address, then two more billion in a single block, so the two-hundred-million-per-block limit that applies to EthenaMinting V2 does not bind this path.

stages.title: Redemption cannot absorb it
stages.action: Issuer-quoted redemption, last-look, twenty million USDe per block
stages.missingDefense: Redemption is collateral-funded and issuer-quoted, not a holder right
stages.explanation: Primary redemption runs through an issuer quote with a last-look check and a per-block contract cap, and it settles against backing assets. Unbacked supply has no backing leg to settle against, so the quote side cannot clear the new tokens at par.

stages.title: Holders take the discount
stages.action: Sell or queue while the unbacked supply is dumped
stages.cost: Minutes per swap, days per unstake
stages.missingDefense: Public exit depth is a fraction of a percent of supply
stages.explanation: On-chain quotes at the pinned block show about 0.8 million in USDC and USDT outputs at nominal par across the main Ethereum pools, against a 4.97 billion USDe supply; these are token outputs, not guaranteed dollars, and deeper pools quote into FRAX or crvUSD. Staked USDe adds a one-day unstaking cooldown before it can even queue for redemption.

defenders.name: Timelocked minter change with a public schedule event
defenders.why: A 24-hour delay and a CallScheduled event are real: the swap is visible before it executes and cannot be executed early or rescheduled silently. It fails as a stop because the proposer and the canceller are the same five-of-ten Safe, the delay cannot be shortened without the timelock's own 24-hour path, and the operation only needs the signatures the attacker already holds.

defenders.name: EthenaSafeGuard on the governance Safe
defenders.why: The guard blocks module enables, fallback-handler changes and non-allowlisted delegatecalls, and requires the relaying executor to sit on a global whitelist. It does not review intent: calling the guard with the exact minter-swap schedule payload passed for a whitelisted executor and reverted for anyone else, so it constrains how the call travels, not whether it goes out.

defenders.name: EthenaMinting V2 per-block mint cap
defenders.why: The 200,000,000 USDe per-block mint maximum is enforced inside the minter contract, not inside the token. Replacing the minter leaves the cap behind, and the fork replay minted twice that amount in one block.

defenders.name: Issuer redemption and last-look quoting
defenders.why: Redemption is an issuer-quoted service that delivers backing assets against burned USDe, gated behind eligibility, a per-block contract cap and last-look pricing. It is not a redemption guarantee against supply that was never collateralised, and the current Reserve Fund is about 1.25% of issuer-reported supply.

defenders.name: sUSDe unstaking cooldown
defenders.why: Staked USDe must cooldown for a day before the underlying can be claimed, which slows holders rather than protecting them. The cooldown is itself a timelocked parameter.

falsifiers.condition: USDe is owned by an address that is not a 24-hour timelock
The timelock's minimum delay is below 24 hours, or a proposer other than the governance Safe exists
The Safe has an independent module, guard owner or second path that can block a signed schedule
A supply or per-block limit binds the token's own mint path
A scheduled minter change has ever been cancelled or vetoed outside the proposing Safe

usdt-tether.title: How does USDT break?
usdt-tether.thesis: Three of six issuer keys can redirect Ethereum USDT's settlement logic immediately; affected holders still need Tether's gated cash exit.
usdt-tether.premise: Hypothetical: three of the six Ethereum issuer-wallet signers are compromised, and a hostile replacement disables settlement before control is recovered. No compromise or misconduct is alleged. This route concerns Ethereum USDT, not an independently verified takeover of every native deployment. A prolonged failure also requires issuer recovery and alternative settlement to fall short; the reserve report does not establish a current shortfall.

stages.title: Take three issuer keys
stages.action: Obtain three confirmations from the six Ethereum issuer-wallet signers
stages.missingDefense: Independent veto above the threshold
stages.explanation: The owner is a legacy three-of-six multisig, not a single externally owned account. On a fork, one and two confirmations left the token unchanged; the third executed immediately.

stages.title: Redirect the token
stages.action: submitTransaction(USDT, 0, deprecate(replacement)) → confirmTransaction → USDT.deprecate
stages.cost: Three signer transactions, no mandatory wait
stages.missingDefense: Replacement validation and timelock
stages.explanation: The token accepts the owner's replacement address without checking its interface or preserving holder rights. A fork replay through the real multisig activated an intentionally reverting replacement on the third confirmation.

stages.title: Transfers stop settling
stages.action: USDT.transfer → replacement.transferByLegacy → revert
stages.missingDefense: Holder-controlled rollback
stages.explanation: A subsequent transfer reached the replacement and reverted on the fork. The original contract also delegates balance, allowance and supply reads; its stored balances do not provide an independent usable exit.

stages.title: DeFi settlement is impaired
stages.action: USDT-dependent withdrawals and swaps encounter the same redirected token
stages.cost: Until settlement or integration is repaired
stages.missingDefense: Independent token settlement
stages.explanation: Aave Core has 2.73B USDT-denominated deposit claims and 84.17M USDT immediately held by its reserve token at the pin. Curve and Uniswap pools share the same token dependency; protocol-level failure propagation is inferred, not replayed end to end.

stages.title: Cash exits remain gated
stages.action: Seek issuer-assisted settlement and direct cash redemption
stages.cost: Verification, issuer processing and redemption fees
stages.missingDefense: Universal direct redemption
stages.explanation: The February 2026 terms make direct redemption personal to verified customers and permit service suspension. The published minimum is $100,000, with the greater of $1,000 or 0.1% charged; the contract's owner-only redeem burns inventory and does not send holders dollars.

stages.title: Recovery fails to arrive
stages.action: Wait for issuer recovery or accept impaired secondary-market claims
stages.cost: Unbounded settlement delay; haircut is not measured
stages.missingDefense: Guaranteed timely recovery
stages.explanation: This catastrophic tail requires Tether's operational response and a working replacement to remain insufficient. A settlement lock does not itself prove reserve insolvency or permanent loss; neither cash redemption nor pre-shock pool quotes guarantees an exit during it.

window.label: Issuer recovery window
window.note: The third confirmation has no waiting period. A legitimate issuer coalition can compete to restore control and appoint working settlement, but no recovery deadline was established.

defenders.name: Uncompromised issuer signers
defenders.why: The remaining three can form a competing threshold coalition, but have no unilateral veto over the attacking three. Wallet owner changes also require the wallet's threshold; success and transaction ordering are not guaranteed.

defenders.name: Token pause and migration
defenders.why: Pause, unpause and replacement selection belong to the same issuer owner. The source permits another replacement, but gives holders no independent rollback; recovery needs issuer control and functioning replacement logic.

defenders.name: Blacklist removal
defenders.why: Removing a blacklist entry does not restore destroyed balances. The fork burned 100,000 USDT and unblacklisting left zero; issuer minting could compensate separately, but no permissionless undo exists.

defenders.name: Verified redemption customers
defenders.why: Eligible customers have contractual cash redemption, subject to minimums, fees and suspension provisions. That access alone does not repair a token that cannot settle transfers to the issuer.

defenders.name: Reserve assurance and audit
defenders.why: The June reserve assurance and announced 2025 financial-statement audit concern off-chain financial reporting. Neither removes Ethereum admin powers or supplies an independent settlement rollback.

falsifiers.condition: Ethereum USDT's owner no longer permits three of the six observed signers to execute the redirect.
The redirect acquires an independently enforceable delay or veto before replacement activation.
The deployed token validates replacement compatibility and preserves an independent holder settlement path.
A tested independent recovery mechanism guarantees timely settlement despite capture of the issuer threshold.
Every holder can obtain direct cash redemption without verified-customer eligibility and the published minimum.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: How does USD1 break?
usd1-world-liberty-financial.thesis: One hot-wallet key mints unlimited USD1 with no cap and no checker; three Safe keys can replace the token's logic outright.
usd1-world-liberty-financial.premise: Hypothetical: the Ethereum hot wallet allowed to mint, or three of the five owners of the ProxyAdmin Safe, are compromised, coerced, or collude. No compromise has been observed. At Ethereum block 26,139,384 the mint path had no cap and the mint checker was the zero address, so one MINTER_ROLE transaction credits any address with any amount, and BNB Chain runs the same governor with single-key minters of its own. Neither Safe has a guard, a module, or an execution delay, and the ProxyAdmin that can replace the implementation holds no timelock. Roughly $4.5bn of USD1 is outstanding across eight chains.

stages.title: Take an operator key
stages.action: Obtain one of the keys that can move USD1: the minter hot wallet, a ProxyAdmin Safe signer, or a freezer wallet
stages.cost: Off-chain key compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.missingDefense: Each operational key is a single point of control
stages.explanation: Hypothetically the attacker holds an operational key rather than a privilege it had to earn. Which key it holds decides the route: an EOA with MINTER_ROLE can mint supply on its own, while a ProxyAdmin signer must still collect two more signatures. No compromise has been observed.

stages.title: Sell into thin pools
stages.action: Swap the new USD1 for USDT, WBNB, and WLFI, and let the secondary price break par
stages.missingDefense: No transfer limit, no circuit breaker, and no par exit for most holders
stages.explanation: The deepest USD1 pair is a BNB Chain 0.01% USDT pool; a static quote at block 126,221,941 returns 991,738 USDT for 1M USD1 but only 2,636,358 USDT for 5M, so the average USDT received per USD1 is already 47% below par. The Ethereum USDT pair returns 104,871 USDT for 1M, and two Ethereum wallets hold 57% of that chain's supply. The last examination covered 2026-08-31, so a shortfall is not visible in a published number on the day it appears.

stages.title: Par exit needs an account
stages.action: Redeem only through a GoAccount under the Stablecoin Services Agreement
stages.cost: Eligibility review, fees, and transaction limits
stages.missingDefense: Direct redemption is closed to non-Accountholders
stages.explanation: The published terms allow only Accountholders to exchange USD1 with the issuer, and the service terms require a registered client in good standing; payment is targeted within two business days and is expressly not a service-level commitment. The issuer reserves the right to set transaction limits and to defer or suspend redemptions, so a holder without an account has a contractual claim it cannot yet exercise.

stages.title: Freeze the venues
stages.actor: Incident response and the operator wallets
stages.action: Freezer role halts balances, pauser role halts the whole token
stages.missingDefense: The freeze and pause keys are single-role EOAs and a WalletSimple
stages.explanation: Freezing the largest exchange wallet took one transaction on the fork, a transfer from that wallet reverted with Account is frozen, and the balance was then drained by the admin Safe and swept out. Pausing the token stops every transfer, including honest exits, and neither action can reverse a mint that already happened.

stages.title: Holders carry the loss
stages.action: Absorb a claim on reserves that no longer matches outstanding supply
stages.explanation: USD1 is a contractual redemption right, not a security interest in the reserve, and the terms disclaim liability for freezes, seizures, and blocked addresses. Exchange balances, pool liquidity, and lending markets priced at par carry the difference.

branches.label: Through the minter hot wallet
branches.premise: The Ethereum hot wallet that holds MINTER_ROLE is compromised, coerced, or colludes. It holds no other role, and its key custody is not established on chain.

stages.title: Take the hot-wallet key
stages.action: Obtain control of the minter EOA
stages.cost: Off-chain key compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.missingDefense: A plain EOA, with no multisig, module, or delay
stages.explanation: This address is not a contract: it has no owners, threshold, guard, or timelock to clear. It signed 59 mints worth 112.6M USD1 between blocks 24,686,176 and 26,136,290, most recently a 7.5M mint about 10 hours before this pin. BNB Chain's governor adds two more single-key minters and a single-key freezer.

stages.title: Mint unbacked supply
stages.action: TokenGovernor.mint(recipient, amount)
stages.cost: One transaction, 89,558 gas on the fork
stages.missingDefense: No cap, no checker, no approval
stages.explanation: The checker slot returned the zero address, so nothing validates a mint, and neither the governor nor the token stores a supply cap. A fork replay of this exact call minted 100,000,000,000 USD1 in one transaction, taking Ethereum supply from 1.61bn to 101.6bn, while a wallet without MINTER_ROLE reverted with OnlyMinterOrBridge.

branches.label: Through the ProxyAdmin Safe
branches.premise: Three of the five owners of the Safe that owns the token's ProxyAdmin are compromised, coerced, or collude.

stages.title: Take three Safe keys
stages.action: Obtain three of five signatures on the ProxyAdmin owner Safe
stages.cost: Off-chain key compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.missingDefense: No guard, no module, and no execution delay
stages.explanation: The Safe is a plain 3-of-5 with an empty module list and a zero guard, and its five owners are EOAs with no further threshold behind them.

stages.title: Replace the token logic
stages.action: ProxyAdmin.upgrade(proxy, implementation)
stages.cost: One transaction, 38,809 gas on the fork
stages.missingDefense: No timelock on the implementation slot
stages.explanation: ProxyAdmin checks only its owner, and the owner is the Safe. A fork replay pointed the proxy at an implementation with the same storage layout; the same call from a random address reverted with Ownable: caller is not the owner, and the Safe's call landed an Upgraded event.

stages.title: Rewrite holder balances
stages.action: Transfer balances straight from holders through the replaced logic
stages.missingDefense: Once replaced, the new logic is the only check
stages.explanation: The replacement implementation could call the ERC20 base transfer directly, bypassing the pause gate and the frozen-account check the shipped logic enforces. On the fork it moved 500M USD1 out of the largest holder and minted a further 1bn, with no role and no signature required.

window.label: From a taken key to a frozen market
window.note: The mint or the implementation swap is one transaction; the market damage and the redemption queue take longer to settle.

defenders.name: Mint checker
defenders.why: The checker slot returned the zero address at the pin, so no contract stands between a MINTER_ROLE call and new supply.

defenders.name: Safe thresholds
defenders.why: Three keys are needed rather than one, but neither Safe has a guard, a module, or an execution delay, and the ProxyAdmin owner is a plain 3-of-5.

defenders.name: Reserve attestation
defenders.why: KPMG examined $4,195,716,067 of reserve assets against $4,195,303,689 of redeemable USD1 for 2026-08-31, which detects a shortfall after the fact; nothing in the mint path reads the attestation.

defenders.name: Freeze and pause roles
defenders.why: A freezer EOA or pauser wallet can halt one venue or the whole token in a transaction, but neither can reverse a mint, and pausing blocks every honest holder as well.

defenders.name: Redemption window
defenders.why: Accountholders can exchange at par through the GoAccount, but the service terms require a client in good standing, target two business days without committing to it, and let the issuer defer or suspend redemptions in a run.

review.note: Both entry routes replayed on an Ethereum fork at block 26,139,384; BNB Chain roles read at block 126,221,941. Awaiting maintainer review of the exact content.

lusd-liquity.title: How does LUSD break?
lusd-liquity.thesis: Nobody holds a key. A broken Chainlink hands pricing to one fallback feed: minting, liquidation and the dollar floor all quote its number.
lusd-liquity.premise: Hypothetical: the Chainlink ETH-USD feed stops returning a usable answer, and the Tellor fallback carries a wrong price while it does. No compromise of either oracle has been observed, and no misconduct by any reporter is alleged. Liquity V1 is immutable: there is no admin key, no pause and no upgrade anywhere in this route, which is why the scenario turns on pricing rather than on authority. Everything else was read or replayed at block 26,139,200 on 2026-10-07.

stages.title: Primary feed breaks
stages.action: latestRoundData() stops returning a usable answer
stages.missingDefense: No second primary feed and no median across sources
stages.explanation: The feed was healthy at the pinned block, answering 2,617.68 dollars with the price feed in its chainlinkWorking state. A reverting, zero or stale answer counts as broken, and the protocol has no other primary source to compare against.

stages.title: Fallback becomes the price
stages.action: PriceFeed.fetchPrice() → _storeTellorPrice(tellorResponse)
stages.missingDefense: No bound between the fallback value and the last good price
stages.explanation: On a fork the fallback value was adopted exactly as reported: the price moved from 2,603.34 to 260.00 in one call with no sanity check on the size of the jump. The caller reads the newest Tellor value directly, with no dispute buffer and no delay.

stages.title: Mint on a false price
stages.action: BorrowerOperations.openTrove(maxFee, LUSDAmount, upperHint, lowerHint)
stages.cost: One transaction, plus the collateral deposited
stages.missingDefense: The 110% rule binds the quoted value, not the market value
stages.explanation: With the price overstated tenfold, one fork transaction deposited 1,000 ETH worth 2.62 million dollars and credited the borrower with 22.76 million LUSD, leaving 11.5 cents of real backing per LUSD received by the borrower. Supply rose from 26.10 million to 48.98 million.

stages.title: Floor pays the quote
stages.action: TroveManager.redeemCollateral(...) at the fallback price
stages.missingDefense: The dollar floor is denominated by whatever the feed says
stages.explanation: Redeeming 100,000 LUSD at a price overstated twofold returned 18.97 ETH, worth 49,658 dollars at the real rate, or 49.7 cents on the dollar. The same redemption at the honest price returned 37.94 ETH, or 99.3 cents. If the error runs the other way the floor closes instead: redemption reverts once the total ratio falls under 110%.

stages.title: Sell into one venue
stages.action: Swap the new LUSD through the Curve LUSD/3CRV pool
stages.missingDefense: One venue carries the float; the rest is dust
stages.explanation: At the pinned block the Curve LUSD metapool held 2.26 million LUSD and quoted five million LUSD out at 5,004,346 USDC on a static-pool basis. Every Uniswap v3 LUSD pool across USDC, USDT and WETH held under 2,000 LUSD. Those quotes assume no arbitrage replenishment and no second venue.

stages.title: Bounded, then repaired
stages.action: Hold through the window, or exit at the discount
stages.cost: The difference between the quote and the market
stages.missingDefense: Nothing reverses what was minted or redeemed in the window
stages.explanation: The price feed returns to Chainlink as soon as both oracles are live, unbroken and within 5% of each other, so the error is not permanent. The transfers made while it was live are. Even after a replayed 22.76 million unbacked mint, the system stood at 391.5% against real prices, so this is a deep discount rather than a collapse of the backing.

window.label: While the wrong number is live
window.duration: As long as the primary feed stays broken
window.note: The fallback publishes about every four hours and was 3 hours 10 minutes old at the pinned block, inside Liquity's own 4-hour freshness limit with about 50 minutes to spare.

defenders.name: Chainlink primary feed
defenders.why: While the primary feed answers, a wrong fallback value changes nothing. On a fork, a fallback quoting 260 dollars left the protocol price at 2,617.68 and liquidation reverted with nothing to liquidate.

defenders.name: Overcollateralisation
defenders.why: The system stood at 724.6% at the pinned block using the Chainlink price, 72,251 ETH against 26.10 million LUSD. That buffer absorbs a large pricing error: a replayed tenfold overstatement that minted 22.76 million LUSD still left the system at 391.5% against real prices.

defenders.name: Immutability
defenders.why: No key can mint, pause, re-point the oracle or upgrade the code, which removes every route the other dossiers turn on. The same property means no one can intervene once a wrong price is live.

defenders.name: Price-feed recovery rule
defenders.why: The feed returns to Chainlink once both oracles are live, unbroken and within 5% of each other, so the mispricing ends with the outage. Trades, mints and liquidations made inside the window are final.

defenders.name: Stability Pool
defenders.why: The pool held 7.57 million LUSD, 29.0% of outstanding debt, and absorbs liquidations before they redistribute. In a false low-price replay it absorbed 68,878 LUSD across 69 troves; it does not address a price that is too high.

defenders.name: Liquity V2 shutdown path
defenders.why: The newer protocol halts a branch on oracle failure instead of pricing from a fallback, which a fork replay confirmed on the wstETH branch. V1 has no shutdown path and cannot borrow this defence.
